title: Your Agent Fix Just Broke Something Else - Sofia Jakovcevic, Arize AI
talk_summary: Arize's Sofia Jakovcevic argues agents fail at runtime, not in the code diff, so regression testing must be built from production traces scored by LLM-as-judge evaluators and gated in CI. She then proposes closing the loop at agent speed: every production failure becomes a regression test, and coding agents get trace access so they can debug and fix themselves.

takeaways.technique: Trace-derived regression suite with LLM-as-judge scoring
takeaways.what_they_do: Pull real production traces into a dataset covering average workflows, known failures, edge cases, and successful workflows to protect; score each run with LLM-as-judge evaluators (task completion, action safety, hallucination, step efficiency) to turn subjective metrics into numeric scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the diff tells you what changed, but the trace tells you what actually happened
takeaways.numbers: Example: +17 points action safety, -17 points task completion, net zero average

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the baseline experiment, apply one change, rerun evals, and wire the whole experiment into CI so each PR must meet regression criteria before merge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't merge until it meets all of the regression criteria that you have listed

takeaways.what_they_do: Before switching to a more expensive model, run the same dataset through both models and compare eval scores to prove ROI numerically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You're not going to switch without proving that you're going to get a good ROI

takeaways.what_they_do: Failed production traces are fed back into the regression dataset, so the suite grows continuously and agents get harder to break.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every failure should become a test. Every failure should make your agents stronger and harder to break

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose observability data to coding agents via skills/MCP so they can see runtime behavior, not just static code, when proposing fixes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're pushing PRs without actually knowing what's happening in production. That means they're pushing PRs blind

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep a small, curated dataset (average workflows + known failures + edge cases + protected successes) rather than synthesizing data, so experiments are fast and representative.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't need to synthesize data. If we already have real user queries
